title: Wipro Plans 10,000-Strong AI Specialist Force With 1,500 Embedded Engineers
excerpt: India's fourth-largest IT company is building a dedicated AI capability, combining new hires, internal transfers and workforce reskilling under a $1 billion investment.
body:
• Wipro is assembling a force of more than 10,000 AI-certified specialists across its operations
  • A dedicated group of over 1,500 forward-deployed AI engineers will be embedded directly with clients
  • The initiative is part of Wipro's previously announced $1 billion AI investment commitment
  • The company has already begun training its 250,000-strong workforce in AI fundamentals

Wipro, India's fourth-largest IT services company, is building an AI capability force of more than 10,000 specialists, including a dedicated client-facing group of over 1,500 forward-deployed engineers who will be embedded directly within customer operations.

The Strategy

The initiative is part of Wipro's previously announced $1 billion AI investment commitment. The company is taking a multi-pronged approach: hiring new AI talent, retraining existing employees and transferring internal resources to AI-focused roles. Available disclosures do not clarify how many of the 10,000 positions represent net new jobs versus internal reskilling and transfers.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=CVX7acmO5DI

The 1,500 forward-deployed engineers represent a particularly aggressive move. Rather than operating from centralized AI labs, these engineers will sit inside client organizations, working directly on implementation projects. This model mirrors the approach taken by consulting firms like McKinsey and Accenture but applied at engineering scale.

Workforce Transformation

Wipro has already begun a broader effort to train its entire workforce of approximately 250,000 employees in AI fundamentals, according to DQ India. The company has partnered with multiple technology providers and academic institutions to build training programmes across skill levels, from basic AI literacy to advanced machine learning engineering.

The scale of the initiative positions Wipro alongside its larger Indian IT rivals. Tata Consultancy Services and Infosys have both announced major AI workforce programmes, though the specifics of each company's approach differ. Wipro's emphasis on forward-deployed engineers suggests a bet on proximity to client problems as a competitive differentiator.

Market Context

The AI push comes as Indian IT companies face pressure to demonstrate relevance in the generative AI era. Clients are increasingly asking their IT service providers to move beyond traditional software development and maintenance toward AI-native solutions. Companies that fail to build credible AI capabilities risk losing market share to both consulting firms and specialized AI startups.

For Indian tech workers, the initiative signals that AI skills are becoming table stakes rather than a specialization. The transition creates both opportunity and anxiety: while AI-trained employees command premium compensation, workers in traditional roles face potential displacement as automation accelerates.

What's Next

Wipro has not disclosed a specific timeline for reaching the 10,000-specialist target or details on compensation structures for AI-specialized roles. The success of the initiative will likely be measured by revenue from AI-specific engagements, which the company has begun breaking out in its quarterly reporting.
